milestones.name: Private GitHub repository created and forward pushed
All six UIs passed the independent App bridge browser harness

events.event: Created the two required timeline files before repository or provider mutation.

Read the execution contract and source plan; refreshed Snacks forward; verified GitHub and Vercel authentication; checked only the SOL targets; froze official source, dependency, protocol, and licensing inputs.
Initialized forward, committed truthful governance and timing records, created the private SOL repository, and pushed the only expected direct bootstrap commit.
Explicit default-branch edit returned HTTP 422 immediately after push; direct reads then proved forward was already the default and only branch.
First branch-protection write returned a provider HTTP 503; follow-up read confirmed protection was not yet applied.
Retried the same bounded protection request after the transient provider failure and verified the enforced no-direct-push policy.
First deterministic Get Time bundle measured 539002 bytes and correctly failed the 524288-byte resource ceiling.
Completed the size-bounded UI adaptation; all six resources measured between 335863 and 354133 bytes.
First strict typecheck exposed the Terser target literal, unchecked manifest indexing, and named mcp-handler export mismatches.
Corrected the four integration type contracts; strict tsc --noEmit passed.
All six current 2026-07-28 and all six legacy Streamable HTTP contracts passed, including isolated tools/resources, ordinary fallback, repeated cycles, and 20 representative clients.
The official ext-apps AppBridge declaration entrypoint failed strict NodeNext resolution because its published declarations use extensionless internal imports.
Isolated the third-party declaration defect behind a narrow typed browser-test runtime shim; strict checking remained enabled and passed.

The first Playwright run exposed a development-only asset routing collision: the screenshot route intercepted the gallery CSS and JavaScript, breaking copy behavior and the 320 px layout. Three additional failures were locator ambiguities in the new test harness.
Repaired development asset fallthrough and stable test locators; all six MCP App UIs initialized in the official AppBridge host and all ten browser/accessibility checks passed.
Typed linting rejected object spread over the full HeadersInit union, correctly identifying unsafe behavior for tuple-array header inputs.
Replaced generic header object spreading with the platform Headers API and reran lint, typecheck, gateway tests, and browser checks.
The first repository secret scan falsely matched the uppercase VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL identifier because the credential-prefix expression was case-insensitive.
Scoped the Vercel credential prefix to its real lowercase token form; the repository-wide scan passed without suppressing token-shaped values.
The production dependency audit passed; the complete audit found the moderate GHSA-48c2-rrv3-qjmp advisory in the direct development YAML dependency at 2.8.1.
Upgraded the exact YAML development dependency to patched 2.8.3 and regenerated the lock and SBOM; the complete audit returned no known vulnerabilities.

The first complete local release:check:ci passed: frozen install, formatting, lint, strict types, 42 Vitest checks, 10 Playwright checks, notices, provenance, architecture, full audit, source and secret scans, SBOM, deterministic resources, public gallery, and production-shaped build.
Committed the coherent green implementation, generated artifacts, tests, security/provenance controls, and truthful running timeline on sol/gallery-v1.
Pushed sol/gallery-v1 and opened ready pull request 1 against forward with the bounded architecture, safety, provenance, verification, limitation, and rollback record.
Release check, CodeQL, locked audit, and public-readiness checks passed on the exact PR head; dependency review skipped because the repository was still private as required by the release sequence.
Vercel rejected Git connection for the private organization repository on the Hobby plan; the project remained correctly configured and manual Preview became the bounded interim path.
An unqualified first Vercel deploy unexpectedly created a Production-target deployment and assigned the stable alias despite project-level automatic-domain controls.
Removed the prematurely assigned stable alias, retained the immutable deployment for auditability, and changed subsequent commands to explicit target flags.
The explicit target=preview deployment became ready at the exact a315b24 PR head after a 70-second provider build.
Direct Preview verification reached Vercel Authentication rather than the application; preserved Standard Protection and selected the provider-supported automation-bypass path.

A diagnostic projection exposed the first automation-bypass secret because Vercel represents it as an object key; revoked and regenerated it before any further proof, then handled only the rotated value in ephemeral process state.

Exact Preview network proof passed all six current and six legacy MCP contracts, public metadata and headers, malformed and oversized boundaries, disallowed methods, and post-abort health. A preceding verifier-only doctype-case false negative was corrected.

All six deployed MCP App UIs initialized and interacted through the independent AppBridge host, but the exact Preview gallery overflowed by 36 pixels at 320 pixels because its full build SHA was unbreakable.

Added safe wrapping for code values and made local browser proof always use a production-length SHA; build, 42 tests, and all ten browser checks passed locally. DEP-002 remains Failed pending a replacement Preview.

issues.expectedBehavior: Explicitly setting the pushed forward branch as default succeeds.
issues.observedBehavior: GitHub returned HTTP 422 immediately after the first push.
issues.rootCause: Repository initialization and branch propagation raced with a redundant edit; GitHub had already selected the only pushed branch.
attempts: Inspected the exact repository
Listed only the exact repository branches
issues.finalCorrection: No mutation required; exact reads proved forward was already default.
issues.closingVerification: Repository view returned default branch forward and branch listing returned only forward.

issues.expectedBehavior: The exact forward protection request succeeds.
issues.observedBehavior: The write returned HTTP 503 and the read returned Branch not protected.
issues.symptom: No server is currently available to service your request.
issues.rootCause: GitHub provider endpoint unavailable for the first exact protection attempt.
attempts: Exact REST protection write
Exact protection read
Bounded retry of the same protection write
Exact closing protection read
issues.finalCorrection: The bounded retry succeeded without changing the intended policy.
issues.closingVerification: Admin enforcement, pull-request requirement, linear history, conversation resolution, no force pushes, and no deletions all reported the intended values.

issues.expectedBehavior: Every deterministic single-file MCP App resource is at most 524288 bytes.
issues.observedBehavior: The first Get Time build was 539002 bytes and failed closed.
issues.symptom: Resource ceiling exception from the bundle generator.
issues.rootCause: The initial Vite configuration used esbuild single-pass minification for a React plus MCP Apps bridge bundle.
attempts: Complete deterministic build using esbuild minification
Three-pass Terser build
Five-pass top-level Terser build
Complete six-app build using a lightweight Chart.js API adapter
Gallery-owned size-bounded adaptations for three React-heavy views
issues.finalCorrection: Retained the frozen upstream audit snapshot, used gallery-owned vanilla MCP Apps adaptations for Get Time, Cohort Heatmap, and Scenario Modeler, and aliased broad Chart.js registration to a bounded canvas implementation for the other chart views.
issues.closingVerification: All six resources passed: 335863, 354133, 337864, 348890, 339570, and 345103 bytes.

issues.expectedBehavior: Strict TypeScript with unchecked indexed access passes.
issues.observedBehavior: The first check rejected four bounded integration type contracts.
issues.rootCause: Initial integration code used looser inferred types and the README export presentation instead of the published declarations.
attempts: First strict TypeScript check
Targeted declaration corrections
Closing strict TypeScript check
issues.finalCorrection: Used the published named createMcpHandler export, explicit public-manifest types, tuple literals for header assertions, and the supported Terser ECMA target.
issues.closingVerification: Strict tsc --noEmit passed with zero errors.

issues.expectedBehavior: The official ext-apps AppBridge entrypoint typechecks under the repository's strict NodeNext configuration.
issues.observedBehavior: The package's declarations referenced extensionless internal modules and failed TS2834/TS2835 before any browser bundle was built.
issues.symptom: Strict typecheck failed inside ext-apps app-bridge.d.ts.
issues.rootCause: The published 1.7.5 AppBridge declaration bundle is not NodeNext-extension-clean even though its browser JavaScript entrypoint is valid.
attempts: Imported the official package entrypoint directly under strict NodeNext
Inspected the frozen upstream bridge implementation and published declaration surface
Introduced a minimal local type boundary that re-exports the unchanged official browser runtime
issues.finalCorrection: Kept skipLibCheck disabled and isolated only the test-host runtime re-export behind a narrow gallery-owned declaration shim.
issues.closingVerification: Strict tsc and the Vite browser-host build passed, followed by all six real-browser AppBridge initializations.

issues.expectedBehavior: The local browser server serves gallery CSS, JavaScript, and screenshots while every UI initializes in the independent AppBridge host.
issues.observedBehavior: The broad screenshot route returned 404 for content-hashed gallery CSS/JS, so copy behavior did not attach and the unstyled 320 px layout overflowed; three other failures were ambiguous accessibility-role locators.
issues.symptom: First Playwright run reported five failures and explicit CSS/JS request failures.
issues.rootCause: The development wrapper intercepted all /assets/:filename requests instead of falling through non-screenshot assets to the Hono application; dynamic role locators also changed identity after UI updates.
attempts: Ran the complete ten-test Playwright matrix
Reproduced failed content-hashed requests in a standalone headless browser probe
Narrowed screenshot handling and stabilized locators against immutable element identifiers
Reran the full Playwright matrix
issues.finalCorrection: Served only known screenshot digests in the wrapper and delegated other assets to the application; used stable CSS/id locators where ARIA role sets legitimately contained multiple live regions.
issues.closingVerification: All ten Playwright checks passed, including six AppBridge hosts, copy/clipboard behavior, keyboard focus, accessible names, alternatives, and 320 px layout.

issues.expectedBehavior: All valid HeadersInit representations are composed without semantic change.
issues.observedBehavior: Typed linting proved that spreading a tuple-array HeadersInit into an object would create numeric keys rather than HTTP headers.
issues.symptom: no-misused-spread failed in error, CORS, and test request header construction.
issues.rootCause: Initial helper signatures accepted the full web-platform HeadersInit union while implementation assumed a plain record.
attempts: Ran type-aware strict linting
Replaced generic error/test header composition with new Headers
Narrowed the internally constructed CORS return type to Record<string,string>
issues.finalCorrection: Used the platform Headers API for union-safe composition and retained record spread only for a function that always returns a record.
issues.closingVerification: Lint, typecheck, 42 Vitest checks, and ten browser checks passed in the complete local release gate.

issues.expectedBehavior: The repository secret scan recognizes real token prefixes without rejecting ordinary uppercase environment identifiers.
issues.observedBehavior: A case-insensitive Vercel-token prefix expression matched VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL in source.
issues.symptom: Secret scan failed on src/base-url.ts despite no credential value being present.
issues.rootCause: The token scanner made the provider prefix case-insensitive even though issued token prefixes are lowercase.
attempts: Ran the repository-wide secret scanner
Inspected only the matching source identifier and scanner expression
Removed case-insensitivity without adding a path or value suppression
issues.finalCorrection: Matched real lowercase Vercel/vcp credential prefixes while continuing to scan the same complete source set.
issues.closingVerification: The scan passed 117 text files and remained part of the green complete release gate.

issues.expectedBehavior: Both production and complete locked dependency audits report no known vulnerability.
issues.observedBehavior: The production audit was clean, but the complete audit reported moderate GHSA-48c2-rrv3-qjmp in direct development dependency yaml 2.8.1.
issues.symptom: pnpm audit reported one moderate stack-overflow advisory with patched version 2.8.3.
issues.rootCause: The initially pinned YAML build dependency predated the advisory's patched 2.8.3 release.
attempts: Ran the production-only audit
Ran the complete JSON audit and reviewed the exact advisory path
Upgraded only the direct YAML dependency to the first patched compatible release
Regenerated the lock and SBOM and reran the complete audit
issues.finalCorrection: Pinned yaml 2.8.3 exactly; no runtime dependency or production behavior changed.
issues.closingVerification: The complete audit returned no known vulnerabilities and the full release gate regenerated the SBOM.

issues.expectedBehavior: The exact Vercel project connects to the exact private GitHub repository and reports a native deployment check.
issues.observedBehavior: Vercel rejected the private organization repository because that connection is unavailable on the current Hobby plan.
issues.symptom: Git repository connection was refused before any linked deployment.
issues.rootCause: Current Vercel plan policy does not allow this private organization-repository connection.
attempts: Connected only the exact SOL repository through the Vercel project configuration
Verified the exact GitHub repository visibility and Vercel project scope
Selected manual protected Preview proof until the authorized public-visibility gate is reached
issues.finalCorrection: Pending: after Preview, security, legal, and public-readiness gates pass, make only this repository public and retry the native connection without plan spend.

issues.expectedBehavior: The first deployment is an unpromoted Preview with no stable alias.
issues.observedBehavior: An unqualified deploy targeted Production and assigned the stable alias despite automatic-domain controls.
issues.symptom: The deployment reported target=production and aliasAssigned=true.
issues.rootCause: The command omitted an explicit target and Vercel selected the new project's Production default; project domain-assignment controls did not suppress the CLI's first-production alias behavior.
attempts: Inspected immutable deployment target and exact Git SHA
Removed only the newly assigned stable alias
Retained the immutable deployment record
Issued all subsequent deployments with an explicit target
issues.finalCorrection: Removed the premature alias and created DEP-002 with explicit target=preview.
issues.closingVerification: The stable alias no longer pointed to DEP-001 and DEP-002 reported no Production target.

issues.expectedBehavior: Automated proof can reach the protected immutable Preview without making its private address public.
issues.observedBehavior: Unauthenticated requests received a 302 Vercel Authentication redirect.
issues.symptom: The application verifier failed before reaching /healthz.
issues.rootCause: Hobby Standard Protection correctly protects generated Preview and deployment URLs.
attempts: Confirmed the redirect without printing the URL
Inspected only non-secret project protection state
Used Vercel's supported automation-bypass mechanism
issues.finalCorrection: Kept Standard Protection enabled and provided the bypass only through ephemeral request headers.
issues.closingVerification: The exact protected Preview passed network and browser requests with the rotated bypass; unauthenticated access remained protected.

issues.expectedBehavior: Protection-bypass diagnostics reveal configuration state without revealing the credential.
issues.observedBehavior: A projected metadata response printed the bypass object key, which is itself the secret.
issues.symptom: The first automation-bypass value appeared in local command output.
issues.rootCause: The diagnostic redacted object values but did not account for Vercel representing automation secrets as property names.
attempts: Stopped using the exposed bypass for proof
Read the official OpenAPI schema for the exact revoke-and-regenerate operation
Revoked and regenerated the bypass
Handled the replacement only in ephemeral shell and process environment
issues.finalCorrection: Rotated the exposed value before further verification and eliminated key enumeration from later output.
issues.closingVerification: Vercel reported a newly created automation bypass at 18:38:26Z; the prior value no longer authenticated subsequent proof.

issues.expectedBehavior: The deployment verifier accepts standards-equivalent HTML doctypes already accepted by local contract tests.
issues.observedBehavior: Budget Allocator failed only because its frozen upstream document uses uppercase DOCTYPE.
issues.symptom: Resource contract false negative after correct MIME, size, and HTML delivery.
issues.rootCause: The deployment verifier used a case-sensitive string prefix while the existing contract correctly used a case-insensitive expression.
attempts: Probed only safe resource metadata and byte length
Aligned the remote assertion with the local standards-insensitive assertion
Reran the complete deployment verifier
issues.finalCorrection: Use a case-insensitive doctype assertion without weakening MIME, size, or document-shape checks.
issues.closingVerification: All six current and all six legacy deployed contracts passed in the complete rerun.

issues.expectedBehavior: The deployed gallery has no horizontal overflow at a 320-pixel viewport.
issues.observedBehavior: The exact Preview document measured 356 pixels wide because each full build SHA was an unbreakable inline code token.
issues.symptom: One of ten deployed browser checks failed while all six App UIs passed.
issues.rootCause: Local browser proof rendered the short development build label, so it did not exercise production-length build metadata.
attempts: Identified exact overflowing elements without printing the Preview URL
Added anywhere wrapping to inline code values
Forced every local browser run to use a 40-character test SHA
Regenerated the content-hashed gallery and reran build and browser checks
issues.finalCorrection: Wrap code metadata safely and make production-length SHA content a permanent browser-test fixture.
issues.closingVerification: Local production-length build metadata rendered at 320 pixels with no overflow; all ten Playwright checks and 42 Vitest checks passed. Replacement Preview proof remains required.
